tr_errors.english: all is pervaded by the nature of reality
tr_errors.problem: direction of pervasion reversed (dharmatā is pervaded by all); the argument is unchanged

tr_errors.english: By listening, beings are liberated.
tr_errors.problem: mnyan pa here means 'ferryman' (ferrymen carry beings across). One symbol in the list is turned into a doctrinal statement about hearing

tr_errors.english: The throne of the heart is endowed with compassion
tr_errors.problem: obscure image translated by guess with no sign of uncertainty

tr_errors.english: to the Guru from Zanglingpa <note>the Copper Isle</note> at Kappura
tr_errors.problem: Kappura/Karpura is probably a recipient's name, not a place (uncertain)

other.note: The opening <meta> is a model-written description of the text ('a commentary on esoteric instructions involving symbolic codes or ciphers'), not a continuity marker

tr_errors.english: The faults of Samadhi arise from perception.
tr_errors.problem: should read 'a samādhi born of ideation is a fault'

tr_errors.english: It was received from the presence of the scholar Naropa and translated at the Pushpahari monastery by the translator Marpa Chokyi Lodro.
tr_errors.problem: in the colophon Nāropa is co-translator with Marpa, not the source of the text; 'rtsigs kyi rgya mdud dang bcas pa' is dropped; 'monastery' is added

tr_errors.english: because the faults and virtues are small, they are gathered
tr_errors.problem: this is the lesser grade of 'warmth' (with faults and qualities), i.e. the path of accumulation; the English makes no sense

tr_errors.english: The seven hundred great qualities
tr_errors.problem: a named stage (Great Expanse) becomes 'seven hundred great qualities'

tr_errors.english: Pulliramale
tr_errors.problem: the name is expanded beyond what the source gives

reader_summary: A volume of the Derge Tengyur tantric commentaries: Mahāmudrā instructions, dākinī symbol-songs and Tilopa's Wish-Fulfilling Jewel. The transcription is the e-text of these Derge leaves, line for line. The English follows doctrinal prose reliably. In obscure images and colophons (translator credits, path stages) it guesses and gives no sign of doubt.
book_verdict: Every leaf has the right text, and the English is readable and mostly faithful. Dense colophons and symbolic verse carry several confident mistranslations, and one page opens with a model-written description inside <meta>.

title: བསྟན་འགྱུར། སྡེ་དགེ། ཚད་མ། ཕེ (Derge Tengyur, vol. 183)
shelf_note: Derge Tengyur, tshad ma vol. phe: a Pramāṇavārttika commentary (identity of pramāṇa and its result, yogic cognition of others' suffering, authorship of the Veda). Correct shelf.

tr_errors.english: wool
tr_errors.problem: snam bu is woven cloth, the whole made of threads. It is rendered 'wool' (a raw material) throughout, which garbles the part/whole example the whole page argues

tr_errors.english: the weaving
tr_errors.problem: thag means loom; loose rendering

tr_errors.english: We see the act and the agent as distinct only in terms of their functional properties.
tr_errors.problem: the sentence runs on to the next leaf; the translator completed it with the opposite claim (the source says 'seen as different in entity...')

tr_errors.english: one accepts being afflicted or not afflicted; at that time
tr_errors.problem: clause garbled

other.note: 'The phrase <note>from the source text</note> states:' is an empty, invented note

tr_errors.english: just like the works of Kumara <gloss>referring to Kumarila or similar young authors</gloss>
tr_errors.problem: gzhon nu 'byung ba is Kālidāsa's Kumārasambhava, the example of a human-authored work. The gloss invents Kumārila, a Mīmāṃsaka, from the opponent's own school

tr_errors.english: because they are a source of valid knowledge
tr_errors.problem: the reason clause is reconstructed loosely

reader_summary: A Pramāṇavārttika commentary from the Derge Tengyur, on perception, valid cognition and the authorship of the Veda. Each leaf has the right transcription. The English follows the shape of the debate, but it mistranslates technical vocabulary and adds glosses with false identifications ('wool' for cloth; Kumārasambhava glossed as Kumārila), so a specialist must check it against the Tibetan.
book_verdict: The leaves are correct and the English gives a usable outline of the argument. Two of the four pages carry a serious error a pramāṇa specialist would catch at once: a key example term mistranslated, and a gloss with an invented identification.

reader_summary: A miscellany volume of the Derge Tengyur: abhidharma on name-and-form, the five factors of killing, ordination aspirations, and protective verses for the directions. Each leaf has the correct transcription. The English is reliable for doctrinal prose, but in lists it reconstructs proper names by guesswork (goddesses, lunar mansions), and one page inserts a false note that text is cut off.
book_verdict: The doctrinal pages are well translated. Name lists are reconstructed by guesswork, and an <unclear> tag claims text is missing when it is not.

reader_summary: A Madhyamaka-section volume of the Derge Tengyur, mostly compendium material on bodhisattva conduct, confession and aspiration. Every leaf has the right transcription, but stray '#' markers from the source e-text are scattered through it. The English is plain and close, the most reliable on this shelf.
book_verdict: The English is good and faithful on all four pages. The transcription pane is littered with '#' markers, some inside words, which a scholar would notice at once; strip them before showing this book.
